This 2015 Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat Has Only 1,259 Miles, Care To Buy It?
12 photos
Photo: Instagram | diamondmotorworks
Is it wrong that some of us still dream about owning a Hellcat ? After all, this model hasn’t been a thing for a few years now, because production of the third-gen Dodge Challenger ended in 2023, after 15 years.
That is also when its four-door sibling, the seventh-gen Charger, was put to sleep, and as everyone and their pet knows, Dodge’s new-age muscle car uses this moniker. The eighth-gen will blow two candles off its birthday cake next month (December 2024). It is made in Canada, and comes either win a twin-turbocharged straight-six engine or with battery-electric power.
However, the V8-powered model is reportedly in the making as Dodge’s way of saying “we’re sorry,” and word on the street is that it could come out at the end of 2027 as a 2028 model year car. That’s roughly one year from now, but the wait should be worth it, because it seems that the Hellcat might be the engine of choice. And if the rumors are correct, then both body styles, the two-door coupe and the four-door sedan, will get the supercharged V8 mill.
It remains to be seen whether it will have the same 6.2-liter displacement as the demised Hellcat versions of the old Dodge Challenger and Charger, as well as the Jeep Grand Cherokee Trackhawk. And speaking of this unit, it is not dead, because it lives on in the Durango and the Ram 1500 SRT TRX.
Photo: Instagram | diamondmotorworks If we were to bet on it, we’d say that it might be an updated version of the 6.2-liter supercharged V8, perhaps with over 800 horsepower. At first, that is, because chances are the company will eventually expand the lineup with all sort of hot muscle cars, and right before pulling the plug on the current Charger, it is possible that Dodge might launch a proper successor to the Challenger SRT Demon 170 .
The latter remains the world’s fastest and most powerful production muscle car to date. It has up to 1,025 horsepower and 945 pound-feet (1,280 Nm) of torque in its top configuration, hitting 60 mph (97 kph) in 1.66 seconds, and running the standing 1/4-mile in 8.91 seconds, at 151.17 mph (243.28 kph). That’s faster than the new Chevy Corvette ZR1X, if you are keeping track of these things.
Now, the muscle car pictured in the gallery is far from being a Demon, let alone a Demon 170, as we are looking at a regular Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat from the 2015 model year. This means that it has 707 horsepower available via the right pedal, channeled to the rear axle through a six-speed manual transmission in this case.
Therefore, the driver engagement factor is definitely there, and interested parties should know that this machine has only 1,259 miles (2,026 km). Thus, it is pretty much brand new. Some of the goodies mentioned in the listing include the Redline Red Tri-Coat Pearl exterior paint finish, black leather interior, Customer Preferred Package 25R, Premium Laguna Leather SRT seats, Harman Kardon premium sound system, and a dual-zone climate control system.
Moreover, this Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat also features HID headlights, an SRT Performance spoiler, a limited-slip differential, 9.5x20-inch wheels, Brembo brakes with red calipers, HID Air-Catcher headlamps, an SRT-tuned Bilstein suspension, parking sensors at the rear, and black vapor chrome exhaust tips, among other things.
Photo: Instagram | diamondmotorworks According to the vendor, which is known as @diamondmotorworks on Instagram, the muscle car in question is offered with two keys, the usual lecture, and a set of floor mats, among other things. The vehicle is in stock and waiting for you to make a move. And before revealing the asking price, we have to tell you that these things do not tend to brake the bank at all.
In fact, one must fork out between $25,000 and some $55,000 for a 2015 model year Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat in today’s used car market in the United States of America. Cars with less than 30,000 miles (48,000 km) on the clock tend to be pricier, whereas those that approach a six-digit mileage are found at the lower end of the spectrum price-wise.
So, how much do you think the pictured 2015 Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat costs? Well, given that it has extremely low mileage, and that it packs plenty of goodies, you already know that it will set you back more than the average muscle car in this configuration, from this model year, don’t you? Without any further ado, you will have to cough out $61,800 if you want to write your name on the dotted line.
Is it worth the asking price? Well, it is if you want a new Hellcat from the 2015 model year, which looks as good today as it did when it initially left the dealership, and if you must really have this one, then you know what to do next, don’t you? But realistically speaking, would you pay almost $62K for and old Dodge? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Diamond Motorworks (@diamondmotorworks)

Father Builds Budget Stealth Camper out of a Cargo Trailer for His Family and It Handles Alaska
16 photos
Photo: Home Sweet Home Alaska | YouTube Screenshot
There are so many ways to approach on-road and camper living that it can be difficult even knowing where to begin. While you can go out there and purchase a new RV, some folks decide to build their own, in the process, choosing precisely how much cash they spend on their dream habitat. Don’t forget the sweat and elbow grease.
Sure, you can spend a bit of cash and acquire a just-add-water camper or RV, as I like to call them – turnkey is the word – or you can craft the habitat of your dreams with as little cash as possible. Today, we’ll be taking a closer look at a unit that’s as affordable as possible, granting its owners access to nothing more than a bed, a heater, a power bank, and some lighting.
Photo: Home Sweet Home Alaska | YouTube Screenshot How this is made possible is with the help of a trailer design that I’ve sworn by time and time again: cargo trailers. Yes, a cargo trailer is what stands at the heart of today’s budget “stealth” camper, and if I may, this solution is one that countless folks who undertake crafting their own RVs call upon; with good reason.
Cargo trailers are often some of the most affordable trailers on the market, and an enclosed one, like what we see here, is a prime choice for building a camper. One reason has to do with the fact that it’s an enclosed, and often, leakproof space, and secondly, they’re designed to handle extra weight, again, standing as a perfect backdrop for wall paneling, wiring, pluming, and whatever else you can think of.
Some folks go really far with their cargo trailer campers , integrating bathrooms into them, complete kitchens, multiple beds, and modular interiors that continue to allow the trailer to be used for cargo, often, fishing gear, e-bikes, and even dirt bikes.
Photo: Home Sweet Home Alaska | YouTube Screenshot Yet some folks, like the people at Home Sweet Home Alaska (HSHA), choose to take a different route, starting their RV and camping journey with a unit that’s as bare as possible, and building it up in time. As a result, at this stage, the solution before us offers very few features. It has what I mentioned above.
Now, the folks over at HSHA chose to build the interior up on their own, starting off with opposing E-tracks along the sidewalls. These tracks are to be the support for a bed system that basically creates a bedding platform suitable for as much as three people, spanning the entire width of the unit.
With the way HSHA created the bedding, suspended on beams that connect to the tracks along the sides, a massive storage area is created underneath. It’s a space that’s large enough for a portable toilet, tools, sleeping gear, fishing rods and climbing gear, even a couple of bikes on their sides.
Photo: Home Sweet Home Alaska | YouTube Screenshot Since this is a bare-bones setup, at the front of the camper, the owners decided to add nothing more than a stand for a diesel heater, and next to it, an Anker portable battery from which to feed the heater the necessary power to make its magic happen, and that’s it. Well, almost.
To ensure that things stay fresh inside and that there’s no CO2 or monoxide poisoning going on, a vent and a detector are added. These are the least you can do for your camping health if you ever build your own camper and want to add heating or cooking systems with gas inside.
Keep in mind that the interior paneling was treated against water, as it is wood, and is the type of material that you don’t want soaking up water or humidity; it’ll rot and you’ll need to change it out.
What I would have liked to know is just how much all this costs, but it’s a piece of information that I either missed or wasn’t mentioned in the clip below. However, we can come up with a rough estimate of how much was spent on this setup .
Photo: Home Sweet Home Alaska | YouTube Screenshot First of all, we have the trailer, which, depending on the model year, where you get it from, and it’s size, you can access for as little $5,000, even less if it’s used. A new model may require that you drop at least $7,000. That’s the trailer part.
Then come the E-tracks, wood, and mattresses, all which can easily fall under $1,000, depending on your level of desired comfort. Toss in a few hundred bucks for the Anker battery bank, a couple more for the heater, and for under $10K, you have yourself the base of what will, in time, become a full fledged RV for you and your family to call upon year after year.
In today’s economy, I wouldn’t be surprised if we see more and more custom builds, ones that people whipped up in their garages and as unique as themselves.

Google Maps on Your Phone's Rear Screen Is the Cool New Feature You'll Get This Year
7 photos
Photo: Xiaomi
The traditional phone form factor might feel like yesterday, following the introduction of the iPhone Duo, but Xiaomi is one of the companies that are trying to improve this design with every generation. The Xiaomi 17 Pro came with a screen on the back in that small bump where your iPhone holds the camera, so the bump wasn’t just a waste of space.
With the Xiaomi 18 Pro now around the corner, this clever design is back in the spotlight. The upcoming model will also sport a display on the back, and according to recent teasers posted by Xiaomi online, it’ll actually be used for some pretty useful things.
One of them is showing Google Maps directions when navigation is active. It’ll also show Spotify and YouTube Music playback controls, so you can just tap the screen to change the song.
For Google Maps, you’ll see your next turn along with the distance to this next turn. As you probably know already, especially if you’re holding a new-generation iPhone in your hand right now, that bump on the back doesn’t allow for a large display, so Xiaomi is trying to use the limited screen estate as effectively as possible.
In case you’re wondering why it would ever make sense to have Google Maps on the back of your phone given you can always run it on the larger, full-size screen on the front, the answer comes down to a different scenario that’s not necessarily related to driving. Instead of using the full screen, which would obviously eat up more battery, you can keep it on the back specifically for those cases when you’re walking around and need instructions to find a destination.
Instead of keeping the entire screen active - when we all know that screens are the number one battery hogs on new-generation phones, especially given they are getting bigger with every new release - you can just run Google Maps on that small display on the back. Sure, you’re not getting a ton of information, but the essential data is there, and you could very well use it for simple things that wouldn’t require the full screen.
Playback controls make even more sense than Google Maps, as you can just see the song name, the artwork, and be able to pause the tune and skip to the next song instantly.
Xiaomi will take the wraps off the new Xiaomi 18 Pro Series on November 17, so we’ll find out more details about this new-generation feature in just a few days. This time, the new model will probably be available worldwide, so you will be able to get your hands on it in most markets.
Photo: Xiaomi Other Google Maps features currently in the works Meanwhile, those whose phones don’t have a screen on the back have other reasons to be happy. One of these reasons is that Google is working on a major overhaul of the experience with Google Maps.
It’s called immersive navigation, and Google itself described it as “ the biggest Google Maps update in over a decade .” It’ll include highly detailed maps with see-through overpasses, 3D buildings, landmarks, sidewalks, crosswalks, trees, and many other details that’ll make the navigation experience feel more realistic.
Gemini is also playing a key role in this new-generation navigation experience. It’ll be in charge of more detailed turn-by-turn directions that will no longer rely solely on distance but will also integrate landmarks to make following a route more straightforward. Gemini will analyze the route, look for landmarks, and update the instructions to include them in next-turn guidance.
Photo: Google A recent patent that autoevolution discovered suggested that Google could evolve this feature with the addition of 360-degree landmarks. With this update, Gemini would provide turn-by-turn instructions that would include landmarks that you can observe from your car even if they’re not necessarily on your route. For example, it can tell you something like “drive in the opposite direction from the stadium” in an attempt to make following the route more straightforward.
The immersive navigation update has already shipped for users in the United States, but the availability continues to be very limited, considering the amount of work and resources involved in this update. However, Google still promised to bring it to more regions as soon as possible, so I expect 2027 to be the year when the immersive navigation update goes live for users in Europe and in other non-American markets.
The update experience will be available on Android and iPhone, but it will also go live on Android Auto and CarPlay in those regions where it is supported. It doesn’t require any change on your device, as Google enables it automatically with a server-side update, so it’s not linked to a specific Google Maps version shipped to your Android smartphone or iPhone.
However, keeping Google Maps up-to-date is always a good idea, including for features such as the ones that will soon debut on Xiaomi’s new flagships. Unlock a new side to your smartphone! With the innovative Back Display, Xiaomi 18 Pro Series brings more imagination, utility, and efficiency to how you use your phone. Never miss what matters. Calls, emails, and important notifications at a glance. Stay on track. Navigation, music, and live activities, updated in real time. Make it your own. Pin text, images, and stickers to your Back Display in just one tap. What's going on your Back Display first? — Xiaomi (@Xiaomi) November 10, 2026

Don't Download "GTA 6 for Free" Because You'll Instantly Regret It
20 photos
Photo: Rockstar
GTA 6 is just around the corner, and unsurprisingly, hackers, scammers, fraudsters- you name it are trying to take advantage of the whole thing in their own malicious ways. This time, they are using a fake GTA 6 for PC free download that ends up with your computer being invaded by malware that does everything from stealing your passwords to extracting crypto information.
An analysis conducted by security company Cynet started with the most obvious thing that has changed in the last few weeks: the number of searches for GTA 6 information.
Keywords like “GTA 6 free download” and “GTA 6 PC download” are becoming more popular, and the bad actors out there know this.
As an early warning, it’s important to keep in mind that GTA 6 for PC isn’t launching yet . Rockstar will only release the game for new-generation consoles, with the PC version expected either next year or at a later time.
People who search for these keywords could end up on a page promising a leaked version of GTA 6 for PCs. Leaked builds are always popular and instantly catch the attention of gamers, and these scams are trying to look as legitimate as possible with GTA 6 artwork , fake security badges, and so on. In plain English, they look almost like the real deal, all in an attempt to convince you to download this fake GTA 6 build.
Photo: Rockstar Games Assuming you end up doing this - at this point, your computer still isn’t compromised - you’re provided with a Google Colab network that points to a GTA 6 EXE file download. This is specifically aimed at Windows computers, and when you click the link, you’re directed to a page where you get more details, supposed to earn your trust and make the whole thing look legitimate.
Oddly, the file size is only 72 MB, but the cybercriminals probably hope that people will think this is just the installer. They also show a download count, a version number, and even fake antivirus checks that indicate the file is clean.
Once you download the executable file and run it on your computer, you pretty much end up opening the door of your PC to the bad actors. The README document that is included in the ZIP archive prompts users to disable the antivirus software installed on their device and run the file as an administrator. This means you’re instructed to let the malicious payload do its job.
Photo: Rockstar Games Gamers eager to play GTA 6 who do this end up getting their computers infected with the WARDEN Stealer, which does all sorts of things, beginning with stealing your passwords, Steam and Roblox credentials, and injecting code into browser processes. Additionally, it can evade virtual machines and sandboxes, so if you decided to run the whole thing in a sandbox to make sure you’re safe, this still wouldn’t be enough to avoid getting infected.
The malicious payload also looks for cryptocurrency wallet details and opens the door for additional malware that can be downloaded and planted in the background.
Eventually, the malicious payload can access anything on your computer and expose it to other infected files that can be downloaded without you even knowing. Your PC is compromised at this point, and all your data, including passwords and cryptocurrency addresses, have left your computer.
Is there anything you can do? Yes. Don’t download these fake GTA for PC builds. It’s important to remember that Rockstar won’t release a GTA 6 build for PC for the time being, and that’s precisely why you shouldn’t search for such a download in the first place.
Photo: Rockstar Games With Rockstar planning to eventually bring Grand Theft Auto VI to PC at some point in the future, there’s a chance these malicious campaigns will return, especially as many people would start looking for ways to get it for free. For now, GTA 6 is only aimed at consoles.
Second, you should never disable your antivirus just because something you downloaded from the Internet tells you to do it. This is a major red flag, and if you pay close attention to everything else, such as the size of the downloaded file and the requirement to run the process as an administrator, everything shows this can’t be good.
The security company says it loud and clear. The downloaded files “contain no game engine, assets, Rockstar signatures, or legitimate GTA functionality.” It’s just a malicious payload that’s trying to trick you into allowing it to run on your computer to steal your data.
November 19 is the big day when GTA 6 will become playable, so these campaigns will continue for a little longer. They will probably continue once other big games come out, so if you really want to play them, just search for legitimate ways to get them. In this case, Rockstar or the official stores are your best options.

2028 Lexus TX 650 Packs the Premium Touch on Top of the Toyota Tundra, Only Across Imagination Land
15 photos
Photo: jlord8 / Instagram
Even in this day and age, when in some regions like North America the days of passenger cars feel numbered because everyone wants only crossovers, SUVs, and trucks, Lexus continues to offer a variety of models for everyone. Well, almost everyone, actually.
They used to have both coupe and convertible models in the roster, but now they rely solely on the compact Lexus IS executive sedan and the larger ES mid-sizer in the passenger car roster. The CUV area is well covered with the UX, NX, RZ, RX, TZ, and TX nameplates. There are also two legacy SUVs packing a tough body-on-frame construction – the mid-size GX and the full-size LX.
But do you know exactly what’s missing and America loves? Yep, trucks, that’s right. North America tried its hand at luxury pickups not long ago and came out suffering, so they didn’t use premium nameplates anymore and instead topped the regular models with premium trim levels that border on insanity in terms of creature comforts and pricing, like the Denali Ultimate from GMC.
Toyota Motor North America has its own equivalent – the 2027 Toyota Tundra Capstone, which starts from $83k sans destination and options! That’s pretty high, right? Alas, it turns out maybe a Lexus pickup truck isn’t a crazy thing. Well, it is, actually, specifically when it’s done for the 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, like the Meso Customs TX1, which started life as a CGI project done by a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators when they were dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI.
Alas, the custom build turned into reality because the aftermarket outlet decided to bring it to life with the looks of a GX and the body of a Tacoma plus ultra-serious off-road chops. However, TMNA would never do it like this. Instead, they might use the larger Toyota Tundra for a simple rebadge featuring the current Lexus tough SUV design language.
That’s the whole idea behind this other virtual project - Jim, a virtual artist known as " jlord8 " on social media, loves messing around with all things CGI from the automotive realm, and he dreams of a Lexus truck that’s called TX 650 and has the face of the GX plastered on top of the Tundra body.
As it turns out, people liked both the color and the interesting CGI mashup. Someone even found its perfect customer base – folks running around between the ranch and the country club. Albeit, it would need an appropriate Lexus-style upgrade to the interior, too, along with a powerful powertrain setup. So, what do you think? Yay or nay for this unofficial, hypothetical design project? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Jim (@jlord8)

The Rovikk Ranger Is an Offroad Teardrop With a Big Surprise in the Back
23 photos
Photo: Rovikk
A teardrop trailer is an excellent solution for those who seek ultra mobility and extra convenience, but let's be honest, it won't do much in terms of personal comfort. The Ranger wants to be an example of a teardrop trailer where mobility, convenience, and heightened comfort
walk
roll hand in hand.
The Ranger is the most popular offroad model from Oregon, U.S.-based Rovikk, formerly known as Teardrops Northwest, or TDNW for short. It's designed as a couple's unit packed with functionality and a superior sense of comfort, apparent inside and out.
That's where the "big surprise in the back" mentioned in the headline comes in. The Ranger comes standard with the nicest, most complete tailgate kitchen you're likely to find in a teardrop. And the surprises don't really stop here, since this model is also impressive for the generous storage options available, the extended autonomy, and overall durability.
Drew Hansen, who runs the popular Playing With Sticks YouTube channel, where he deals mostly in lightweight and compact trailers, names the Ranger the best replacement for the now-discontinued Escapod Topo 1 teardrop and pretty much near perfect on its own. You don't have to take his word for it, but the extended video tour at the bottom of the page might convince you to.
Photo: Rovikk The video below showcases several Ranger builds and a smaller Scout. Its purpose is to highlight the fact that these trailers are customizable to a large extent, though also pretty neat in standard configuration.
The Ranger has a 5 by 9-foot (1.5 by 2.7-meter) footprint and sits on a sturdy, tubular steel chassis riding on all-terrain BFG tires. Standard equipment includes a 3,500-lb Timbren HD axle-less suspension, 12-inch brakes, as well as a full wheel and tire mounted on the side, so you have a trailer that will go off the beaten track whenever you feel like it.
The shell is anodized aluminum in standard spec , but you can add a wrap like on the units you see below, whether a single color or graphics. The standard layout offers an 80-inch (203-cm) bed inside with ample storage on both ends, regardless of where you want to have the head of the bed.
Photo: Rovikk Rovikk offers two choices for cabinetry layouts insides, one with a pass-through to the rear galley (Cheslow option) and another with more cabinets but no pass-through (Quadra). Both are shown in the video tour.
Whatever your option, Rovikk promises you a space with a comfortable, large sleeping area and a spot for every item so you won't be tripping over them. It's a nice upgrade over a traditional teardrop, which will have, at most, a shelf overhead for storage.
That said, the biggest surprise of the Ranger is the tailgate kitchen , imagined as a full U-shaped chef's unit when it's deployed at camp. Here, too, you have options to choose from in terms of the number and shape of drawers, as well as colors and types of wood used.
Photo: YouTube/Playing With Sticks/Drew Hansen Rovikk structures the galley in three rows, plus the standard formica counter and a clip-on table with a foldable sink and water pump on the side. These rows include CNC-machined cabinets with metal pulls and hinges, full-extension drawers with metal locks to keep everything in place during transport, and larger cubbies.
They also include two slide-outs on either end, one for a cooler box or fridge, which can be customized to fit a unit you already have or are planning on getting, and the other for the Camp Chef cooktop. The latter sits on top of a larger cubby for pots and pans and integrates a second extension that reveals an additional working surface .
Rovikk doesn't describe the galley of the Ranger as a Swiss-army-knife-type of tailgate kitchen, but they might as well. It's not just surprisingly large and smartly design, but also very mindful to include every-day functionality.
Photo: YouTube/Playing With Sticks/Drew Hansen Standard here are a pair of 2.9-gallon (11-liter) Dometic Go jugs that will hook up to a Dometic Go collapsible sink and water pump, an LED strip, overhead lights, and the electric panel. Adjustable latches secure everything in place when it's time to hit the road again.
Also part of the standard equipment, you get reverse lights and a 2-inch bike receiver to which you can mount a swing-out bike rack so you'll be able to use the kitchen without having to take the bicycles off.
The Ranger comes standard with steel Jeep-style stand-on fenders, a pair of roof racks, a poly box on the tongue for batteries and storage, a 100Ah battery that you can use as the basis of a(n optional) solar array, a jockey wheel, a skid plate, and Max Coupler. A MaxxAir roof fan, a vapor barrier underneath, a rock guard, rotating rear stabilizer jacks, fluorescent underbody lights, and 110V/12V/USB outlets are also included standard.
Photo: Rovikk Rovikk describes it as rugged, durable, "bold and capable," and a complete solution straight out of the factory. You can also upgrade it or even go full custom by simply toggling through available options, which adds extra appeal.
Dry weight is 1,850 lbs (839 lbs), with maximum carrying capacity set at 3,500 lb by the choice of suspension. Base price is $25,999 and will stop wherever your demands or budget halts.

EICMA 2026 • MTPeak Stole Some of the Spotlight at EICMA 2026 With Insane Power and Retro Looks on Three Wheels
These Designers Took a Crack at Building a Cargo E-Bike and Came Up With a Neat Utility Concept
14 photos
Photo: Tzu-How Chang | Eric Lee | FENG-YUE LEI | Nonnon YN Ho | An-Pin Chiu
Ah, the timeless bicycle, a vehicle that has been subject to so many spin-offs and approaches that we can write an entire book on the matter. With the arrival of electrification, this undying vehicle has gone under even more transformations.
Since stresses on e-bike frames are a bit different than on traditional ones, we’ve come to design bicycles differently these days. Some brands have even gone further and set their sights on the urban landscape, giving rise to wild frame designs that break the mold of what we’re used to. Dive even deeper, into let’s say, cargo bikes, and traditional frame cues go out the window.
Photo: Tzu-How Chang | Eric Lee | FENG-YUE LEI | Nonnon YN Ho | An-Pin Chiu For example, cargo e-bikes are available in two major styles, long tails, and long necks, as I like to call the latter. The former extends the rear of the bike in order to create a space where we can load up cargo, often, in the form of grocery baskets or seats and footrests for carrying children.
As for longnecks, they’re often denoted by an extended front end that places a large platform or basket at our disposal, and allowing for larger items. I’ve seen people carry other bikes on such a variation.
But, in between the lines of bicycle mechanics and styles, some brands and garage crews have explored some of the more obscure cues of design, giving rise to bikes that break the mold when compared to traditional ones.
Photo: Tzu-How Chang | Eric Lee | FENG-YUE LEI | Nonnon YN Ho | An-Pin Chiu Such a concept, exploration, or disruption of timeless styling and bicycle construction is called OUO, a two-wheeler aimed at the urban landscape and all about “utility.” Every single corner of the bike is aimed at doing something, so to speak, even calling upon a look that very few other bikes have been designed around.
For instance, the OUO is built with a U-shaped down tube that forms the head tube, BB, and seat tube. To help bring in some compliance or lateral strength, two top tubes connect the head tube, seat tube, and flow into the seat stay.
What I found rather neat about OUO is that the space between your legs, an area that is often left to no use, can be used for storing things like a laptop, some documents, or anything that can fit between those sidepanels.
Photo: Tzu-How Chang | Eric Lee | FENG-YUE LEI | Nonnon YN Ho | An-Pin Chiu More on the cargo side of things, the front and rear of the OUO are capable of carrying goodies. At the front, a tray is in place, a feature that’s spotted on quite the array of European bikes on the market, often, helping secure your essentials with the help of bungee cords, and at the rear, a classic pannier system is in place.
While the designers showcase no bags, we could easily add a couple and drape them over the sides of the rear wheel, as long as they don’t touch the ground; it appears as though 20-inch wheels are used for the OUO. It’s also not clear if this rack can support another person too, but probably can’t.
As for the rest of the bike, we don’t much about it as the ideation page makes no mention of what’s in store here, but what I found most interesting is that the minds and hands behind the OUO did take the concept all the way into a working concept.
Photo: Tzu-How Chang | Eric Lee | FENG-YUE LEI | Nonnon YN Ho | An-Pin Chiu There’s a little video below that shows it in action, and if I may, this means that the OUO is but a step away from production; the designers just need to secure a contract and sell the rights to a brand. Maybe they start it on their own.
While there are no details on the secondary gear of the OUO, we can see some of what’s in store. At the front, a suspension fork is in place, placing some bump-reducing action at our fingertips, but the rear is a stiff one, so we’ll be relying only on the cross-section of the tire to reduce vibrations.
In terms of electronics, a motor is spotted on the rear wheel, so it’s a hub-drive e-bike, and the battery pack, because the frame has no place to put it, is located on the seat tube, as it extends well into the saddle. It doesn’t look like the largest pack on the market, more like a range extender, but it should grant us access to at least 50 km of riding, maybe even more if it boasts more than 275 Wh of juice like most extenders.
Photo: Tzu-How Chang | Eric Lee | FENG-YUE LEI | Nonnon YN Ho | An-Pin Chiu Braking is handles by a pair of hydraulic clampers with four pistons each, granting us more stopping power than most e-bikes on the market, and if you ask me, essential for staying in control, especially with cargo on the bike.
Personally, I’m liking what the designers of OUO have done here, and if I may, for the right price, I’d bite. It’s compact, nimble, and actually looks decent for a twisted framework of pipes that break the mold of traditional bicycle design.

Dealer Selling New Chevy Corvette ZR1, Markup Will Leave You Speechless
8 photos
Photo: Instagram | limitedspec
Can you believe it’s been almost two and a half years since Chevrolet pulled the wraps off the all-new ZR1 version of the C8-generation Corvette?
Well, the model premiered in mid-2024, boasting more oomph than the original Bugatti Veyron. The latter model is considered the world’s first hypercar, and its famous W16 engine with quad turbocharging was officially rated at 987 hp (1,001 ps/736 kW). The 8.0-liter unit, which was paired with a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission and all-wheel drive, rocketed it to 60 mph (97 kph) in roughly 2.5 seconds, which was definitely a jaw-dropping achievement for something that hit the assembly line in 2005.
By comparison, the C8 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 is some two-tenths of a second faster, while costing a fraction of the price. More on the Benjamins in a few moments, as first, we have to remind you that the American hypercar has 1,064 horsepower to play with. This comes out to 1,079 metric horsepower and 794 kilowatts. The peak thrust is officially rated at 828 pound-feet (1,123 Nm), and power comes from the Z06’s engine, which has been equipped with two turbochargers in this case.
Chevy’s modern-day Corvette ZR1 can complete the standing quarter mile in 9.6 seconds at 150 mph (241 kph), the spec sheet reveals, and if you keep the right pedal pinned to the floor, then it will eventually top out at 233 mph (375 kph). If you want quicker sprints, then you may want to opt for the ZR1X version of the car. The top speed may be identical to the ZR1, but the 0-60 mph acceleration is dealt with in a whopping 1.89 seconds. This model takes 8.99 seconds to run the standing 1/4 mile at 157 mph (253 kph).
Photo: Instagram | limitedspec As for the firepower, it too features the same 5.5-liter V8 with twin turbocharging. However, the C8 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1X also boasts electric assistance sourced from the E-Ray that is now dead and buried. In total, you are looking at a neck-snapping 1,250 bhp. That’s 1,268 horses for the metric crowd and 933 kilowatts. The powertrain develops 937 pound-feet (1,270 Nm) of torque in total. This means that the ZR1X can give modern-day supercars a real run for their money.
Speaking of the finances, a brand new Chevy Corvette ZR1X from the 2027 model year will set you back a minimum of $227,800. This means that it is a lot more affordable than the Lamborghini Temerario, not to mention a heck of a lot faster. In fact, it can beat the larger, punchier, and more expensive Revuelto, too. Well, at least in a straight-line acceleration, according to the spec sheet.
However, we wish you good luck if you want to buy one for a little over the MSRP, because you’d have more chances of finding a needle in a haystack due to the insane markups. The same goes for the Chevy Corvette ZR1 , which officially starts at $198,000 for the latest model year, the bowtie brand’s official US website reveals.
On average, the 2025 to 2027 model year cars tend to fetch between just under @250,000 and over $320,000 in today’s used car market. The latter sum is obviously reserved for barely driven examples from the latest model year, which feature plenty of optional extras, such as the ZTK Track Pack, and the former will get you an earlier model year that has seen some action and does not pack that may goodies.
Photo: Instagram | limitedspec The pictured Chevy Corvette ZR1 is looking for a new home as we speak. The selling dealer behind it, which is known as @limitedspec on Instagram, has not revealed the model year. However, it did reveal that this machine has only 360 miles (580 km) under its belt. Therefore, it a new ride, hence the ultra clean look inside and out, as you can see for yourselves in the images shared in the gallery.
This ride features a glossy black look on the outside, sits on black Y-spoke alloys that spin around the red brake calipers, and has a mostly red interior, albeit with a few black touches here and there for some contrast. Carbon trim is also on deck, alongside the familiar screen setup, a flat-bottom steering wheel with a red 12 o’clock marker, and no wall of buttons, to no one’s surprise, because that was a thing on the pre-facelifted C8.
Strangely, the dealer did not have much to say about this Chevy Corvette ZR1 , as you are about to see in the social media post embedded at the bottom of the page. However, it did reveal that this American hypercar is located in Miami, Florida, and as you can imagine, it costs a lot of money. At the time of writing, the asking price was $299,980, which is actually more than the ZR1X’s MSRP.
Therefore, if you believe that this C8 ‘Vette is worth $300K, then you know what to do next, don’t you? But would you really fork out that much money for this ride? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Limited Spec Automotive (@limitedspec)

Everest Four-Season Truck Camper Proves This Flagship Solution Can Be All the RV We Ever Need
25 photos
Photo: Host Campers
The camping lifestyle can be approached in so many ways that we can easily get lost in all the solutions. However, if there’s one that literally means no limits, it’s the truck camper, the ones we load up onto the rear of our trucks and delve as deep into the wild as our running gear will allow.
Sure, travel trailers are nice, and motorhomes even more so, but one glamping solution has been called upon time and time again, and if you’re aware of the limits we can reach with a truck camper, then you’re aware of why they’re often a common choice for traveling adventurers.
Unlike motorhomes, a truck camper doesn’t include a vehicle but is most often loaded up onto the rear of your existing one. Sure, there are some brands out there that sell a truck camper with the vehicle too, but most don’t, allowing us to call upon whatever solution fits in our bed in order to start exploring ASAP.
Photo: Host Campers Truck campers also differ from travel trailers in that, because they’re mounted to the rear of our trucks, allows us to explore where standard towable habitats can’t. Again, running gear is the main reason behind this.
Yet, there is a limit that truck campers are clearly under rule from: size. Since those solutions are often dropped onto the rear of a truck, they’re designed and built to ensure that we affect maneuverability as little as possible, which clearly limits just how large a truck camper can be.
Limited space means, well, limited space, and because of this, most truck campers only allow for around two to three people to rest their heads at night. Sometimes, by calling upon a roof-top tent, the capacity can be extended to two extra guests.
The lack in space not only affects sleeping accommodations, but all accommodations and creature comforts, including the size of living areas, kitchens, and the presence of a bathroom, if any. That’s where Host Campers and their Everest comes in.
Photo: Host Campers The Everest is the truck camper before you today, a solution that breaks the limits that truck campers are known to abide by, and in doing so, is able to offer a space that’s much larger than the average, and the way it does this is by calling upon a trait often reserved for larger motorhomes, RVs, and some travel trailers: slideouts.
Yes, the Everest uses slide-outs to craft a space that’s large enough to accommodate the lifestyle of up to five guests. This model is also considers Host’s flagship model, the one that they used to first display their triple-slide know-how; three slides are in place, in case I need to be clear here. Host does build other triple-slide behemoths, and we’ve shed light on some of them before.
Now, three slides does something, and as you’d expect, it expands the interior living space to well beyond what your average truck camper can. As a result, Host is able to literally stuff the belly of this unit with all that we need to live a comfortable life.
Photo: Host Campers As mentioned, up to five guests can be accommodated here, and all five also have a place to sleep, made possible by a modular dinette, elevated forward and cab-over bedroom, and a modular sofa. If you’re aware of what we usually find in an RV of this nature, you’re already know that we’re already stretching the limits of what’s possible.
Still, because of the use of slide-outs, Host is able to also add a complete kitchen inside this camper, along with cooktop, microwave, sink with faucet, and large fridge, suitable for all those guests. But, there’s a bathroom inside this unit too, and one that splits the toilet and vanity to one side, and in the middle of the camper, a shower stall.
Without sounding too much like a commercial , “wait, there’s more,” and that more is found in the shape of systems like heating and cooling, solar and shore power connectivity, entertainment options, and ample storage to stuff the habitat full of the gear and clothing we need to live off the land for as long as we wish.
What I also liked about the Everest is that it has one of the largest fresh water capacities of RVs, campers, and motorhomes on the market, bringing forth 65 gallons of the stuff to support your off-grid activities. Oh, and because of the way the shell is built, the Everest is a four-season camper.
Photo: Host Campers Keep in mind that what we see does weigh 3,890 lbs (1,764 kg) in its lightest form, so if your truck can’t handle at least 4,000 lbs, you should look at smaller options. Not to mention that you will need to own a truck with a long bed.
Now, this little introduction into the Everest is just that, an introduction, and in if I was to go through all that this unit has to offer, we’d be here until the cows come home, so be sure to dive in deeper if what you see has caught your interest. There’s a little clip below for some more insight.
As for pricing, again, Host creates the Everest as a year-round glamping solution, and these are rarely inexpensive, so expect a bit of a premium for these compact and family-ready beasts. According to some dealers, we can pic up a 2026 Everest for around $90K, so clearly not cheap.

2027 BMW M350 xDrive Enters the CGI Beast Mode, Comes Out Slammed and Widebody But Still Elegant
6 photos
Photo: ildar_project / Instagram
The premium Bavarian automaker BMW has been making the rounds lately with its brand-new series of Neue Klasse novelties, and while many have already been presented, like the second-gen iX3 and i3 sedan or the all-new X5 and 3 Series, many more are scheduled to arrive soon.
The upcoming novelties may or may not include, according to the rumor mill, a V8-powered BMW Alpina grand touring coupe, the BMW i3 Touring, Alpina’s luxury sedan , or the high-performance M3 and M3 Electric plus X5 M and iX5 M crossover SUVs, plus many others.
Alas, it seems that people are now fixating on just one of the numerous novelties: the BMW M Performance M350 xDrive sedan. With 437 horsepower, BMW's latest elite sedan delivers near-M3 performance minus the latter’s quirks and high price.
Of course, it’s not cheap, either, but at least it brings a breath of fresh air to those who can’t stand the current BMW M3 and M4’s ‘nostrils’ – aka the double-coffin kidney grille. BMW launched the G50 all-new 3 Series a few months after the all-electric i3 sedan, and while they share many parts and the general looks, the regular compact executive sedan is arguably the better-looking half.
That’s mostly thanks to slightly changed proportions thanks to the added wheelbase and the fact that the M350 xDrive comes with M Performance goodies off the factory floor, plus an enhanced turbocharged inline-six, which is now more powerful than the M3 from two generations ago!
So, it’s no wonder that folks have taken a liking to it – including the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI. For example, Ildar, the virtual artist better known as " ildar_project " on social media, usually plays with tuned vehicles - so is anyone surprised by this new creation?
Actually, the pixel master feels a bit fixated on the new BMW M350 xDrive because he’s done variations of this unofficial, hypothetical design project before, in white with black touches and also in green with the same black details. There's even a menacing all-black setup he calls 'Cobra.'
But now he’s after a crimson setup, and while the black elements are still there, he mixes the slammed attitude and exotic widebody treatment with a set of elegant gold wheels to mix and match with the yellow LED daytime running lights.
So, what do you think of this treatment? Do you believe it is worthy of this BMW, and do you think it reminds us of the good old days from the Need for Speed age of digital customization, even though the Bavarians look firmly into the future with the Neue Klasse styling DNA?
